---
title: "Simulation (paper), step 7: extract the estimates for the evaluation"
---

Step 7 of the paper simulation: extract the estimates, truths and fit diagnostics that the evaluation
(`S3_Code_Simulation_Coverage.Rmd`) needs into small files, joined with the truths.

**Selection** (95 % QI only; point estimate = median of the bootstrap or posterior draws)

| Design | Estimand | Methods | Truth |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ML | marginal pooled / grouped (superpopulation) | slide bootstrap (pooled, grouped); Binomial + Poisson; Multinomial; Wilson (pooled recall and precision) | `02_truth_superpopulation.csv` |
| Pathologists | average pathologist (pooled / grouped) | row, cluster and two-way bootstrap; Binomial + Poisson (new pathologists); Binomial + Poisson (observed pathologists, as in Example 1) | `02_1_truth_average_pathologist.csv` (population of pathologists) |
| Pathologists | single pathologist (pooled / grouped) | stratified and cluster bootstrap; Binomial + Poisson | `02_1_truth_new_pathologists.csv.xz` (20,000 per-pathologist truths) |

- ML design: scenarios A-D.
- Single pathologist: the share of the per-pathologist truths inside the interval (and below / above
  it) is computed here, so the evaluation does not need the 20,000 truths per scenario and variant.

**Output: data of the evaluation** (project root, next to `S3_Code_Simulation_Coverage.Rmd`)

- `S3_Data_ML_Estimates.csv.xz`: `scenario`, `n_slide`, `rep`, `variant`, `method`, `method_id`,
  `averaging`, `name`, `value`, `.lower`, `.upper`, `truth`.
- `S3_Data_Pathologist_Estimates.csv.xz`: `scenario`, `n_slide`, `rep`, `variant`, `estimand`,
  `method`, `method_id`, `averaging`, `name`, `value`, `.lower`, `.upper`, `truth` (average
  pathologist), `share_inside`, `share_below`, `share_above` (single pathologist).
- `S3_Data_Objects_per_Image.csv`: mean number of objects per image (`mean_P`) of the
  superpopulation per scenario.

**Output: fit diagnostics** (`simulation/results/`)

- `07_ML_diagnostics.csv.xz`, `07_pathologist_diagnostics.csv.xz`: fit diagnostics of the Bayesian
  models (divergences, maximum tree depth hits, max Rhat, min bulk and tail ESS).

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(readr)
```

# Settings
```{r}
dir_results <- "simulation/results"

# Methods of the evaluation
ml_bayes_models        <- c("binomial_poisson", "multinomial")
pathologist_bootstraps <- tribble(
  ~estimand,             ~model_id,
  "average_pathologist", "bootstrap_row",
  "average_pathologist", "bootstrap_cluster",
  "average_pathologist", "bootstrap_two_way",
  "single_pathologist",  "bootstrap_stratified",
  "single_pathologist",  "bootstrap_cluster"
)
pathologist_bayes_models <- "binomial_poisson"
```

# ML design
```{r}
df_truth_superpop <- read_csv("simulation/data/02_truth_superpopulation.csv",
                              show_col_types = FALSE)

# Slide bootstrap: pooled and grouped
df_ml_bootstrap <- read_csv("simulation/estimates/06_bootstrap_estimates.csv.xz",
                            show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(interval == "qi", averaging %in% c("pooled", "grouped"))

# Bayesian models: marginal (superpopulation) estimates. Only the needed columns are read
# from the large file.
df_ml_bayes <- read_csv("simulation/estimates/05_bayes_estimates.csv.xz",
                        col_select = c(scenario, n_slide, rep, variant, model, model_id, estimand,
                                       averaging, name, interval, value, .lower, .upper),
                        show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(interval == "qi", estimand == "marginal", model_id %in% ml_bayes_models)

# Wilson interval: pooled recall and precision
df_ml_wilson <- read_csv("simulation/estimates/06_wilson_estimates.csv.xz",
                         show_col_types = FALSE)

bind_rows(df_ml_bootstrap, df_ml_bayes, df_ml_wilson) |>
  left_join(df_truth_superpop, by = c("scenario", "variant", "name", "averaging")) |>
  select(scenario, n_slide, rep, variant, method = model, method_id = model_id,
         averaging, name, value, .lower, .upper, truth) -> df_ml_estimates

# Datasets per method, averaging and metric (expected: 4,000 per scenario A-C, 3,000 for D,
# 15,000 in total; Wilson pooled recall and precision only)
df_ml_estimates |>
  distinct(method, averaging, name, scenario, n_slide, rep, variant) |>
  count(method, averaging, name, name = "datasets")
```

# Pathologist design
```{r}
df_truth_average <- read_csv("simulation/data/02_1_truth_average_pathologist.csv",
                             show_col_types = FALSE)
df_truth_new     <- read_csv("simulation/data/02_1_truth_new_pathologists.csv.xz",
                             show_col_types = FALSE)

df_path_bootstrap <- read_csv("simulation/estimates_pathologists/06_1_bootstrap_estimates.csv.xz",
                              show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(interval == "qi") |>
  semi_join(pathologist_bootstraps, by = c("estimand", "model_id"))

# Observed pathologists (as in Example 1): a further method for the average pathologist, compared
# with the truth of the population of pathologists
df_path_bayes <- read_csv("simulation/estimates_pathologists/05_1_bayes_estimates.csv.xz",
                          show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(interval == "qi", model_id %in% pathologist_bayes_models) |>
  mutate(
    observed = estimand == "observed_pathologists",
    model    = if_else(observed, paste(model, "(observed pathologists)"), model),
    model_id = if_else(observed, paste0(model_id, "_observed"), model_id),
    estimand = if_else(observed, "average_pathologist", estimand)
  ) |>
  select(-observed)

df_path <- bind_rows(df_path_bootstrap, df_path_bayes) |>
  select(scenario, n_slide, rep, variant, estimand, method = model, method_id = model_id,
         averaging, name, value, .lower, .upper)
```

Average pathologist: the truth of the population of pathologists. Single pathologist: the share
of the 20,000 per-pathologist truths inside, below and above the interval (with the sorted truths
per scenario, variant, metric and averaging).
```{r}
df_path_average <- df_path |>
  filter(estimand == "average_pathologist") |>
  left_join(df_truth_average, by = c("scenario", "variant", "name", "averaging"))

df_path_single <- df_path |>
  filter(estimand == "single_pathologist") |>
  nest(intervals = -c(scenario, variant, name, averaging)) |>
  left_join(df_truth_new |>
              group_by(scenario, variant, name, averaging) |>
              summarise(truths = list(sort(truth)), .groups = "drop"),
            by = c("scenario", "variant", "name", "averaging")) |>
  mutate(intervals = map2(intervals, truths, \(df, truths)
    df |>
      mutate(
        share_below  = findInterval(.lower, truths, left.open = TRUE) / length(truths),
        share_above  = 1 - findInterval(.upper, truths, rightmost.closed = TRUE) / length(truths),
        share_inside = 1 - share_below - share_above
      )
  )) |>
  select(-truths) |>
  unnest(intervals)

bind_rows(df_path_average, df_path_single) |>
  select(scenario, n_slide, rep, variant, estimand, method, method_id, averaging, name,
         value, .lower, .upper, truth, share_inside, share_below, share_above) -> df_path_estimates

# Datasets per estimand, method and averaging (expected: 600 each)
df_path_estimates |>
  distinct(estimand, method, averaging, scenario, rep, variant) |>
  count(estimand, method, averaging, name = "datasets")
```

# Fit diagnostics
```{r}
df_ml_diagnostics <- read_csv("simulation/fits/04_fit_diagnostics.csv.xz",
                              show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(model_id %in% ml_bayes_models)

df_path_diagnostics <- read_csv("simulation/fits_pathologists/04_1_fit_diagnostics.csv",
                                show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(model_id %in% pathologist_bayes_models)

list(ml = df_ml_diagnostics, pathologists = df_path_diagnostics) |>
  map(\(df) df |>
        select(scenario, n_slide, rep, variant, model, model_id, divergences, max_treedepth_hits,
               max_rhat, min_ess_bulk, min_ess_tail, error)) -> diagnostics

# Fits per model (expected: 16,000 per ML model for A-D, 600 pathologist fits) and failed fits
diagnostics |>
  map(\(df) count(df, model, failed = !is.na(error)))
```

# Objects per image
Mean number of objects per image of the superpopulation per scenario; the evaluation orders the
scenarios and image counts by the expected number of objects per dataset (mean P x images).
```{r}
read_csv("simulation/data/01_slides_superpop.csv.xz", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  group_by(scenario) |>
  summarise(mean_P = mean(P)) -> df_objects_per_image

df_objects_per_image
```

# Save
```{r}
dir.create(dir_results, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Data of the evaluation (S3), next to S3_Code_Simulation_Coverage.Rmd. xz-compressed csv
# (readr compresses by the file ending, about 6 times smaller); read_csv() reads the files directly
write_csv(df_ml_estimates,      "S3_Data_ML_Estimates.csv.xz")
write_csv(df_path_estimates,    "S3_Data_Pathologist_Estimates.csv.xz")
write_csv(df_objects_per_image, "S3_Data_Objects_per_Image.csv")

# Fit diagnostics
write_csv(diagnostics$ml,           file.path(dir_results, "07_ML_diagnostics.csv.xz"))
write_csv(diagnostics$pathologists, file.path(dir_results, "07_pathologist_diagnostics.csv.xz"))

# File sizes in MB
file.info(c(list.files(pattern = "^S3_Data_"), list.files(dir_results, full.names = TRUE)))["size"] / 1e6
```
